$comment:
The description of every migration, keyed by its VERSION (the three-digit filename prefix),
which is the migration's identity in public.schema_migrations. The slug after the number is
informational and may change; the version may not.

db/MIGRATIONS.md is GENERATED from this file plus the files actually on disk
(`npm run db:docs`). Edit descriptions here, never in the generated block.

A new migration with no entry here renders a MISSING marker and fails
tests/migrations-doc.test.mjs, so a migration cannot be merged undocumented. That test is
the replacement for the hand-kept list that silently stopped at 017 and omitted five
migrations and ~1,370 lines of DDL.

nonMigrations.016_isolation_tests.sql: A **test**, not a migration. It creates two throwaway orgs, asserts every cross-tenant write is rejected, and deletes its own data. Run it after the sequence and confirm `✔ ALL ISOLATION TESTS PASSED`. This is why the migration numbering has no 016 — and why the gap is declared here rather than being a hole the runner has to guess about
nonMigrations.migrations-ledger.sql: The ledger table itself (`public.schema_migrations`). Applied idempotently by `npm run db:migrate` before every run, so a database that predates the ledger can still be brought under it. Not numbered, because it must be able to run before migration 001 and can never itself be pending
nonMigrations.GO-LIVE.sql: **Deprecated — do not run.** A byte-identical concatenation of 012 + 013 + 014 + 015, made as a one-shot for a deployment that had already applied 001-011. It is now many migrations stale and is not self-standing (it aborts on a fresh database because `accept_invitation()` does not yet exist). Retained only so an operator who used it can identify what they applied

descriptions.001: **Baseline.** Core tables, enums, RLS on every table, functions, triggers, indexes, the integer-minor-unit money model and the no-double-book exclusion constraint. Formerly `db/schema.sql`; renamed so it sorts first and can carry a ledger identity
descriptions.002: Item cost + image; job-photos storage policies
descriptions.007: Job/billing address, message templates, job tasks/equipment/checklists
descriptions.008: Item title/taxable/photo, price book, deposits, document customisation, archive
descriptions.009: Leads + booking RPCs, technician field tools, invoice online-pay columns
descriptions.011: Recurring plans, reminder log, review URL
descriptions.012: Custom job statuses, job stage/tags/expenses, commission %
descriptions.013: Fixed `search_path`, EXECUTE lockdown, booking rate limit, `webhook_events` policy
descriptions.017: Helcim connected accounts, provider-neutral payments, payment settings
descriptions.018: Per-member permissions, industry onboarding, device subscriptions
descriptions.019: Dispatch crews, custom fields, automations, operations, growth, customer portal
descriptions.021: Job actions, warranties, callbacks, call tracking
descriptions.022: Appearance, last-owner protection, finance/tax/settlement, privacy/retention, platform admin
descriptions.024: Links invoices to their originating estimate so deposits are credited
descriptions.025: Stops jobs with a null `end_date` haunting the dispatch board
descriptions.026: Aligns the currency constraint with what the payment layer can process
descriptions.027: Indexes the lookups the app makes on every request
descriptions.028: Extends the no-double-book guarantee to crew (`job_assignments`), not just the lead
descriptions.029: `booking_settings.timezone` — booking slot maths runs on the business's clock, not the server's
descriptions.030: Refund ledger, derived refunded_minor, refund permission, and the audit trail payments never had
descriptions.031: Tips, ACH release holds, payment schedules/milestones, org default deposit, booking deposits
descriptions.032: Automation-run uniqueness, per-recipient campaign delivery claims, and outreach send tracking
descriptions.033: Append-only stock ledger, derived `inventory_items.quantity`, concurrency guard, multi-line purchase orders with a receive step
descriptions.034: Push event tracing, the support-access audit table, and an `accept_invitation(token)` that actually requires the emailed token
descriptions.035: Guards `custom_field_values.entity_id` (audit F21 — polymorphic, no FK, no org check); adds opt-in `organizations.tax_mode` and `document_tax_context()` so tax jurisdictions and customer exemptions can price a document
descriptions.036: Credit notes and void (the original document and its NUMBER are kept), safe max-aware document numbering with a release-on-failure compare-and-set, the edit lock on sent/signed/paid documents and their line items, and a `version` column on both document tables. **Requires 030** — it refuses to run without `can_refund_payments()`
descriptions.037: `deleted_by` on the four soft-deletable tables (backfilled from `audit_log`), the restore-consistency and privacy-erasure triggers behind `/trash`, and indexes for listing deleted rows
descriptions.038: Request-context evidence for e-signatures (`document_signature_events`, `approve_document_with_evidence`), login attempt throttling and logging (`auth_login_attempts`, `record_login_attempt`, `login_throttle_counts`), an audit trail for role and capability changes (`permission_change_log`), per-profile security state, and `secret_key_rotations` so `PAYMENT_SECRETS_KEY` can be rotated without orphaning stored Helcim tokens. Additive: drops nothing, and preserves 023 §6's `signed_at is null` guard on `approve_document` verbatim
descriptions.039: Technician pay rates and labour costing, time off, skills, estimate options, appointment tokens
descriptions.040: Staff notification inbox (claim + audit), the dunning ladder's per-rung claim, sent statements, **calendar feed tokens bounded like 023 §10's portal tokens** (NOT NULL expiry, revocation, scope), report schedules with a per-period delivery claim, the bulk-operation failure record, and accounting-export idempotency. Additive: drops nothing
descriptions.041: The bilingual trade catalogue in the database, `job_types.name_en/name_he/pack_item_key`, a sync trigger that maintains the Hebrew booking-service name instead of copying the English one, a re-runnable `repair_booking_service_names()`, the pack menu for businesses that chose trades and have **no** job types (an org that already has any is skipped entirely), and an empty default for `organizations.job_types` so 005's HVAC list seeds nobody new. Additive: drops nothing
descriptions.042: **Security fix.** Restores `and voided_at is null` to `approve_document_with_evidence`. Migration 036 §11 added that guard so a VOIDED document could not be signed from its old public link; migration 038 replaced the function with the evidence-capturing version, carried the sign-once guard across VERBATIM and silently dropped this one. Between 038 and here, anyone holding the public token of a voided estimate or invoice could sign it into an approved, signed document. Found by executing db/ci/ for the first time (ledger 0.6). Replaces one function; drops nothing.
